result:
All three solutions give 16, and I checked the parts that matter.

**The upper bound (16) holds.** Each signed determinant corresponds to a vector in the six permutation-monomial coordinates. I verified Solution 1's identity coordinate by coordinate: per(Z) = ½(D₁ + D₂ + D₃ − D₄) on all six monomials. Expanding the product gives 4·4 = 16 terms.

**The lower bound is the hard part.**
- The set of signed-determinant coefficient vectors is exactly the 32 sign vectors with product −1. This follows from the GF(2) rank of the permutation/cell incidence matrix being 5.
- Solution 2's Lemma 1 (at least four factors are needed to write p = (1,…,1) in this set) has a flaw: its counting argument ignores repeated columns. I checked the three-factor case directly with a parity argument, and it is impossible, so the conclusion survives.
- Solution 2's Lemma 3 projection is valid. I verified that the map φ sends D ∩ W into D ∩ W₀, which reduces any 5-dimensional factor to a 4-dimensional one without changing k.
- With both factors reduced to rank 4, the column spaces are coordinate subspaces with exactly 4 pairs of ±d_i, and the (i,j) entries must all be nonzero. This forces at least 16 terms.

Lemma 2's case analysis is only sketched, so the lower bound is not fully verified here. Still, it is the most detailed and mostly checkable argument. Solution 1 asserts its lower bound without proof. Solution 3 relies on unverifiable "exact mixed-integer programming" claims and gives no argument.

Solution 2 is the strongest of the three.

CHOICE: 2
